drafts.title: Front seats provide longer thigh support and reliable memory restoration
drafts.description: Customers can extend front-seat thigh support for taller drivers and rely on the seat memory to restore their saved position reliably on first use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front-seat cushion includes an adjustable thigh-support extension adjustable by at least 60 mm from the retracted position; seat memory restores the saved seating position on the first recall in >=95% of attempts when tested across 200 uses per vehicle under normal temperature conditions.
assumptions: 60 mm additional extension provides meaningful benefit for tall drivers and is mechanically feasible within successor architecture.
Seat memory reliability is measured after vehicle start and without manual override, using a 200-cycle bench test per vehicle sample.
Battery/vehicle electrical health is within normal operating parameters during tests.
uncertainties: Interaction with optional seat cushion shapes or third-party aftermarket covers may affect perceived thigh support.
Extreme temperatures could affect seat motor behavior; this requirement targets typical operating range.

drafts.title: Cup holders accept common bottle and travel-mug sizes
drafts.description: Customers can place commonly used water bottles and travel mugs in the vehicle's cup holders and expect them to fit and stay secure during normal driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept cylindrical container bases up to 85 mm diameter and secure them against tipping at lateral accelerations up to 0.5 g; validated with a representative set of 10 common bottle and travel-mug shapes.
assumptions: 85 mm covers the vast majority of common single-use bottles and large insulated travel mugs.
Validation uses standardized fixtures and inertial tests to simulate cornering and braking.
uncertainties: Extremely large or irregular-shaped containers (non-cylindrical bases) may still not fit.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with expanded color and brightness choices and per-zone customization
drafts.description: Customers can choose from a wide palette of ambient-light colors and brightness settings and configure lighting by zone to match mood or preference.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 selectable colors, a minimum of 10 distinct brightness steps, and per-zone customization across at least 4 interior zones (front doors, rear doors, dashboard, footwell); user can save at least 3 presets.
assumptions: RGB LED-based lighting is used to deliver the color palette and brightness steps.
Zones are visible to the user in the lighting settings menu and can be configured independently.
uncertainties: Exact perceived color may vary with interior trim materials; calibration will be required for different trims.

drafts.title: Rear seating space at least as generous as main competitors
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers experience legroom that is competitive with the segment's main rivals when front seats are positioned for taller occupants.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear knee clearance (industry-standard knee point to seatback) is equal to or greater than the arithmetic average of the vehicle's main competitors when measured with front seats set to the 95th-percentile occupant position; validated in a laboratory measurement against three named competitor vehicles selected by product planning.
assumptions: Product planning will nominate the three main competitors for the comparison at development start.
Measurements use the industry-standard method for knee-point to seatback clearance.
Front seats remain in their standard factory track limits (no aftermarket adjustment).
uncertainties: Competitor dimension changes between development start and launch could affect the comparison; product planning will freeze competitor set at a defined milestone.

drafts.title: Exterior access systems work reliably in cold weather and hands-free entry is responsive
drafts.description: Customers can enter the vehicle and open the tailgate reliably even in freezing conditions and expect the hands-free tailgate gesture to open the boot quickly on first attempt.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles operate reliably (unlock and open with gloved hand) at ambient temperatures down to -25°C without manual defrost in >=95% of attempts; hands-free tailgate opens after a valid kick/wave within 2.0 seconds on the first attempt with a success rate >=95% under normal conditions (no obstructions), validated across 200 attempts.
assumptions: Testing uses standard winter test procedures and representative gloves.
Hands-free tailgate detection is tested with common footwear and in typical parking configurations without heavy snow/ice accumulation on the boot area.
uncertainties: Extreme ice buildup or mechanical blockage (e.g., frozen seals) may still prevent operation; this requirement targets normal freezing conditions.

drafts.title: Physical volume control that allows accurate adjustment without looking
drafts.description: Customers can change audio volume using a physical control quickly and accurately without needing to look at the screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Users can reach a target volume change using the physical volume control without looking in <=2 seconds in >=90% of trials during a standardized user test (n=50 participants across typical hand sizes).
assumptions: The test scenario uses the most common target adjustments (e.g., single-step up/down and change of 6 dB).
Haptic feedback or detents are available to support non-visual operation.
uncertainties: Exact user success may vary with hand size and glove use; test includes a representative sample.

drafts.title: Trunk supports powering a portable cooler for customer use
drafts.description: Customers can power a portable cooler from the vehicle's trunk to keep items cold during trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The vehicle provides an integrated trunk power outlet or purpose-built power interface that allows a portable electric cooler to operate continuously for at least 4 hours at 40 W consumption under nominal vehicle electrical conditions; outlet is accessible without removing stored cargo.
assumptions: Typical portable coolers draw ~30–50 W; 40 W is representative for test purposes.
Continuous operation is validated with the vehicle in accessory mode or vehicle running as per customer expectation.
uncertainties: Higher-power aftermarket devices may not be supported; customer guidance will note supported power envelope.

drafts.title: Provide 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder for the volume knob (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested the volume knob use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder; this is a component-level specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder as requested in customer feedback (12-bit resolution).
assumptions: This draft captures a specific component-level wish from customers.
Final engineering feasibility, supplier selection and integration are out of scope for product requirement definition.
uncertainties: Implementation details (connector, firmware handling, redundancy) require engineering analysis.
drafts.scope_reason: Component-level engineering specification requested by customers; engineering implementation, supplier selection and technical integration are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Side window glass thickness: 4.5 mm laminated (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested side windows use 4.5 mm laminated glass; this is a component-level engineering request.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Side windows are specified as 4.5 mm laminated glass per customer request.
assumptions: This draft captures a specific material/thickness request from customers.
Structural, NVH and weight impacts require engineering evaluation.
uncertainties: Safety and crash behavior, glazing supplier availability, and weight implications must be validated by engineering.
drafts.scope_reason: Material/thickness specification is a component-level engineering request; structural and safety implications are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Seat cushion foam density: 55 kg/m³ (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat cushion foam with a density of 55 kg/m³; this is a component-level engineering specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Seat cushion foam is specified to use foam with a density of 55 kg/m³ as requested.
assumptions: This draft records a specific material density request from customers.
Comfort perception and durability trade-offs need engineering validation.
uncertainties: Durability, weight, and supplier availability implications must be assessed by engineering.
drafts.scope_reason: Material/component density specification is an engineering-level request; detailed validation and trade-offs are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Meet new EU pedestrian protection regulation (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the vehicle front end meet the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle front-end design complies with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation applicable at time of homologation.
assumptions: Regulatory text and interpretation at homologation time will determine exact measures required.
uncertainties: Regulatory changes prior to launch may alter technical requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance and homologation requirements are out of scope for product feature definition and must be handled by compliance engineering.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification request (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers requested that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear-seat airbags achieve FMVSS 208 certification as required by US regulations at time of vehicle certification.
assumptions: Certification depends on regulatory test procedures and engineering validation.
uncertainties: Certification outcomes depend on crash test results and may require design changes.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory certification requests are out of scope for product requirements and fall under compliance engineering.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern follow ECE R112 in every market (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that headlights follow ECE R112 beam-pattern rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Headlight beam patterns meet ECE R112 requirements where applicable; compliance to be demonstrated at homologation in each target market.
assumptions: Market-specific regulations and approvals determine final beam patterns.
uncertainties: Some markets have different or conflicting headlight regulations; resolution requires regulatory guidance.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance and homologation are out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business/pricing request)
drafts.description: Customers requested a BMW-guaranteed residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request recorded: customers ask for a 60% residual value guarantee after five years.
assumptions: Residual-value guarantees are a commercial/financial decision requiring business-level agreement.
uncertainties: Execution depends on dealer programs, financing structures and market conditions; out of scope for product technical requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Price/financial guarantees are out of scope for product requirements; they belong to commercial/finance teams.

drafts.title: Request to cut production cost per car by 8% (business request)
drafts.description: Customers requested BMW cut production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request recorded: customers ask for an 8% reduction in production cost per car.
assumptions: Production cost targets are a business/engineering trade-off requiring company-level decisions.
uncertainties: Impact on feature set, materials and supplier choices must be assessed by program management and procurement.
drafts.scope_reason: Production cost targets and commercial trade-offs are out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Provide a 12 V trunk outlet (component-level request)
drafts.description: Customers explicitly requested a 12 V socket in the trunk to run a cooler box; this draft captures the component-level specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A dedicated 12 V trunk socket is specified as requested in customer feedback.
assumptions: This draft captures a customer-specified component; electrical integration, fusing and power budget must be validated by engineering.
uncertainties: Actual rated current and power delivery require electrical-system design and safety validation.
drafts.scope_reason: Voltage and socket-specification requests are component-level engineering specifications; detailed electrical validation is out of scope for product requirements.
